4 MapSketch include sketch showing the t: North-oriented map of a 3.5-mile operational radius covering Blackwood Industrial Park, Blackwood River Mile Marker 42, and State Route 104. The primary site is Storage Tank #4 at Apex Chemical Tank Farm, MM 42.1 on the East Bank, where a shell fracture is leaking concentrated Styrene Monomer. Impacts include heavy chemical sheening on 1,200 meters of river and an 800-yard VOC plume extending East-Northeast across Route 104. The Blackwood Municipal Drinking Water Intake at MM 39.1, 3.0 miles downstream, and Blackwood Marsh Ecological Reserve, 1.5 miles downstream, are threatened. A USCG auxiliary drone observed a 200-yard-wide slick moving South-Southwest at 1.8 knots and moderate east-bank shore oiling. Shoreline impacts extend across riprap and mudflats from MM 42.1 to MM 41.3. Show Staging Area A at Westside High School, Boom Sites 1 and 2, the Mobile Command Post at County Fire Station 12, the 500-foot Exclusion Zone, and intake protection zones.
5 Situation Summary and Health and Safet: At 06:45, a catastrophic Tank #4 seal failure released approximately 8,500 gallons of Styrene Monomer into secondary containment, with overflow entering the river through storm drain outfall #3 at about 30 gpm. A vapor cloud crossed Route 104, causing road closure and evacuation of 60 industrial properties. Hazards include styrene inhalation toxicity, narcotic and central-nervous-system effects, respiratory irritation, flammability at an 88°F flash point, dermal burns, steep-bank falls, and heat stress at 91°F. Enforce a 500-foot Exclusion Zone; require Level B PPE with SCBA and PID/LEL/O2 monitoring in the Hot Zone and Level C with full-face organic-vapor APR in the Warm Zone; continuously monitor the command post and downwind baselines; and operate wet decontamination at Facility Gate 2.
7 Current and Planned Objectives: Maintain life safety and the 500-foot exclusion perimeter by 08:00; complete containment booming at Boom Site 1 (MM 41.5) by 10:30 to protect the drinking water intake; secure the Tank #4 leak and complete product transfer by 12:00; continuously monitor air along Route 104 and publish public safety advisories by 11:00; and transition to Unified Command by 10:00.
ActionsRow1: County Fire Engine 12 and Hazmat 1 were dispatched to establish the 500-foot perimeter.
ActionsRow2: Chief Henderson established Local Command, initiated facility emergency shutdown, and closed Route 104.
ActionsRow3: Regional Hazmat Team 4 arrived, began perimeter PID monitoring, and established decontamination at Gate 2.
ActionsRow4: The USCG Sector Strike Team and EPA On-Scene Coordinator arrived and established Unified Command at Fire Station 12.
ActionsRow5: Spill Response Vessel River Guardian deployed 1,000 feet of hard containment boom at MM 41.5, Boom Site 1.
ActionsRow6: Entry Team 1 enters the Hot Zone in Level B PPE to secure the Tank #4 bottom manifold valve.
ActionsRow7: Deploy a secondary sorbent deflection boom array at Boom Site 2, MM 40.2, upstream of the drinking water intake.
ActionsRow8: Begin vacuum-truck skimmer recovery of pooled styrene at storm drain outfall #3.
